paths.title: Git, Commits & Pull Requests
paths.description: Keep AI-assisted work reviewable, attributable, reversible, and safely integrated through disciplined version-control practices.

lessons.title: Start from a current base
lessons.principle: Old branches accumulate avoidable conflicts and stale assumptions.
lessons.practice: Fetch or sync before beginning consequential work.

lessons.title: Use a focused branch
lessons.principle: A branch should represent one coherent change.
lessons.practice: Keep unrelated features, fixes, generated assets, and experiments separate.

lessons.title: Inspect the working tree first
lessons.principle: Pre-existing local changes can be overwritten or accidentally committed.
lessons.practice: Check status and diff before an agent begins modifying files.

lessons.title: Stage intentionally
lessons.principle: AI tools may touch more files than expected.
lessons.practice: Review changed files and hunks before staging rather than blindly adding everything.

lessons.title: Write meaningful commits
lessons.principle: Commit history is an engineering communication channel.
lessons.practice: Use concise messages that describe intent and keep each commit understandable.

lessons.title: Keep commits buildable where practical
lessons.principle: Broken intermediate history complicates bisecting and review.
lessons.practice: Group changes so important commits preserve a coherent state.

lessons.title: Review the diff before commit
lessons.principle: Generated output can include accidental deletions or formatting churn.
lessons.practice: Inspect behavior-changing lines, dependency changes, migrations, and generated files.

lessons.title: Avoid unnecessary force pushes
lessons.principle: Rewritten shared history creates coordination risk.
lessons.practice: Use force-with-lease only when branch history intentionally needs rewriting.

lessons.title: Keep PRs small
lessons.principle: Review quality declines as diff size grows.
lessons.practice: Split large initiatives into independently valuable, mergeable slices.

lessons.title: Write a useful PR description
lessons.principle: Reviewers need intent and verification context.
lessons.practice: Describe problem, solution, notable decisions, risks, migration impact, and tests.

lessons.title: Link requirements to changes
lessons.principle: A PR should make it easy to verify whether scope is satisfied.
lessons.practice: Reference issue or acceptance criteria and explain any deviations.

lessons.title: Expose generated changes clearly
lessons.principle: Reviewers need to know which files are generated versus authored.
lessons.practice: Document generation commands and avoid hand-editing outputs.

lessons.title: Call out migrations and dependencies
lessons.principle: These changes carry outsized operational risk.
lessons.practice: List new packages, lockfile changes, schema migrations, and rollout requirements prominently.

lessons.title: Use draft PRs early
lessons.principle: Early PRs provide CI and collaboration without claiming completion.
lessons.practice: Open drafts for large changes and transition to ready only after validation.

lessons.title: Require current-head validation
lessons.principle: A green check on an older commit is not evidence for the latest code.
lessons.practice: Merge only when required checks apply to the exact head being reviewed.

lessons.title: Resolve review threads deliberately
lessons.principle: Comments represent unresolved reasoning, not boxes to click.
lessons.practice: Address, explain, or explicitly reject feedback before resolving threads.

lessons.title: Re-review after material changes
lessons.principle: A PR can become substantially different after fixes.
lessons.practice: Request or perform another review when architecture, security, or behavior changes significantly.

lessons.title: Protect the default branch
lessons.principle: Direct unreviewed changes undermine delivery controls.
lessons.practice: Use branch rules, required checks, and appropriate approvals for production repositories.

lessons.title: Use safe merge strategy
lessons.principle: Merge, squash, and rebase have different history consequences.
lessons.practice: Choose the repository's intended strategy and preserve important authorship or context.

lessons.title: Verify after merge
lessons.principle: Integration can trigger deployment or environment-specific failures.
lessons.practice: Confirm default-branch CI, deployment, migrations, and smoke checks after merge.

codeExamples.snippet:
git status -sb
git diff
git add src/service.ts test/service.test.ts
git diff --staged
git commit -m "Fix duplicate project creation"

## What changed
- Prevent duplicate project creation
## Risk
- touches idempotency path
## Validation
- unit + integration tests
- manual retry scenario

paths.title: Code Review & AI Review
paths.description: Review generated changes for behavior, architecture, security, maintainability, and evidence rather than accepting plausible-looking code.

lessons.title: Review intent before syntax
lessons.principle: Correct-looking code can implement the wrong requirement.
lessons.practice: Start by comparing the diff to the task and acceptance criteria.

lessons.title: Review behavior-changing lines first
lessons.principle: Formatting noise should not consume the same attention as logic.
lessons.practice: Prioritize control flow, state changes, queries, permissions, network calls, and persistence.

lessons.title: Trace data flow
lessons.principle: Security and correctness issues often cross file boundaries.
lessons.practice: Follow important inputs from entry through validation, transformation, storage, and output.

lessons.title: Check authorization at the server
lessons.principle: Client-side hiding is not an access-control mechanism.
lessons.practice: Verify every sensitive operation enforces permissions in trusted code.

lessons.title: Check error handling
lessons.principle: Generated code often under-specifies failure behavior.
lessons.practice: Look for swallowed errors, broad catches, fail-open logic, missing rollback, and unusable messages.

lessons.title: Check async behavior
lessons.principle: Missing awaits and stale closures create subtle defects.
lessons.practice: Inspect concurrency, cancellation, retries, cleanup, and race-prone state.

lessons.title: Check dependency changes
lessons.principle: A one-line import can pull significant risk.
lessons.practice: Verify package identity, necessity, version, license, and maintenance.

lessons.title: Check duplicated logic
lessons.principle: AI may solve locally by copying an existing pattern imperfectly.
lessons.practice: Search for authoritative existing utilities or services before accepting duplication.

lessons.title: Check architectural boundaries
lessons.principle: A feature can work while making the system harder to evolve.
lessons.practice: Look for new cross-layer imports, cycles, global state, or database access in inappropriate layers.

lessons.title: Check types and schemas
lessons.principle: Type escape hatches can hide contract errors.
lessons.practice: Scrutinize casts, any-like types, ignored errors, optionality, and schema mismatches.

lessons.title: Check tests for false confidence
lessons.principle: Tests can mirror the implementation and miss the real contract.
lessons.practice: Ensure tests cover acceptance, failure, permissions, and realistic integration.

lessons.title: Check accessibility
lessons.principle: Visual review alone misses interaction defects.
lessons.practice: Inspect semantics, focus, keyboard behavior, labels, and state announcements.

lessons.title: Check performance impact
lessons.principle: Generated loops and queries can scale badly.
lessons.practice: Look for repeated work, N+1 requests, unbounded lists, heavy client bundles, and missing caching rationale.

lessons.title: Check observability
lessons.principle: New critical behavior should be diagnosable.
lessons.practice: Verify safe logs, metrics, traces, or audit events for important operations.

lessons.title: Use AI as a second reviewer
lessons.principle: An independent model can surface issues the authoring model missed.
lessons.practice: Ask a reviewer agent to inspect the diff adversarially with the spec and repository instructions.

lessons.title: Do not treat AI review as approval
lessons.principle: Automated review is fallible and context-limited.
lessons.practice: Validate AI findings and retain human ownership for consequential merges.

lessons.title: Review generated configuration carefully
lessons.principle: CI, infrastructure, permissions, and deployment files can create broad effects.
lessons.practice: Inspect every privilege, secret reference, trigger, environment, and destructive command.

lessons.title: Review deletions and renamed behavior
lessons.principle: AI can remove code it believes is unused.
lessons.practice: Confirm callers, compatibility, migrations, and feature flags before accepting removal.

lessons.title: Review the final head
lessons.principle: Earlier review does not cover later fixes.
lessons.practice: Perform a final diff and check review after all requested changes are applied.

lessons.title: Write review conclusions
lessons.principle: High-value review records why the change is acceptable.
lessons.practice: Summarize tested behavior, remaining risks, follow-ups, and any consciously accepted tradeoffs.

codeExamples.snippet:
git diff --stat main...HEAD
git diff main...HEAD -- src/ test/
npm test
npm run typecheck

Review order:
1. Requirement match
2. Authorization/data flow
3. Failure behavior
4. Tests
5. Performance
6. Accessibility
7. Diff scope
